incentives.name: Data center retail sales and use tax exemption
incentives.what: Exempts computer equipment and enabling software bought or leased for qualifying data centers that meet capital investment and job thresholds; runs through 2035. The 2026-2028 budget (law June 29, 2026) left it in place.
incentives.value_known: About $928 million in forgone state and local tax in FY2023 (JLARC); about 90 percent of the industry uses it.

incentives.name: JLARC review of the exemption
incentives.law: JLARC report, Data Centers in Virginia (2024)
incentives.what: State audit agency found the exemption cost about $928M in FY23 and gave options: extend, let expire in 2035, or replace with a partial exemption through 2050.

laws_and_bills.name: 2026-2028 budget: data center electricity consumption tax
laws_and_bills.what: Tax of $0.011 per kWh on electricity used by data centers, effective July 1, 2026, capped at $600M a year statewide, expires after June 30, 2028; SCC to issue guidelines within 60 days. Did not repeal the sales tax exemption.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 30 (2026 Senate budget): end data center sales tax exemption Jan 1, 2027
laws_and_bills.what: Senate proposal to end the exemption eight years early; dropped in the final budget compromise.

laws_and_bills.name: HB 30 (2026 House budget): conditions on the exemption
laws_and_bills.what: House proposal to keep the exemption only if data centers remove co-located fossil generation by July 1, 2027, meet clean energy targets 10 years early and install Tier 4 backup generators by 2031; not in the final budget.

local_rules.what: Digital Gateway rezonings (about 1,790 acres) voided by Circuit Court (Aug 2025) for faulty public notice; affirmed by the Court of Appeals Mar 31, 2026; project ended Jul 2, 2026.

Phase 1 of the Data Center Standards and Locations amendments (CPAM-2024-0001, ZOAM-2024-0001), approved Mar 18, 2025: data centers no longer allowed by right; they need a rezoning or Special Exception. Applications accepted before Feb 12, 2025 may be grandfathered. Phase 2 (use-specific standards for data centers and substations) is underway.

Board voted Sept 15, 2026 to move toward a pause of up to 12 months (the most Virginia law allows) on final Board action on data center and substation applications that need legislative approval; administrative (by-right) applications are not covered; exceptions possible for grid-reliability substations and applications near their legal decision deadline. Final resolution set for Oct 20, 2026, retroactive to Sept 15.
Code amendment approved Feb 24, 2026 ends by-right data centers; a Special Use Permit with public hearings is now needed in all Office, Commercial and Industrial districts.

Ordinance O-2026-455: data center standards in the I-1 and I-2 districts (pre-construction noise studies, facade variety, screened generators and HVAC, bigger setbacks from homes, parks and childcare). Passed first reading unanimously Feb 9, 2026; second reading not confirmed.
Outright data center moratorium adopted in June 2026 (per law firm summary).
Board directed staff to draft zoning amendments removing data centers as a by-right use, ending the by-right framework of the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District.
Board directed staff to draft zoning ordinance amendments removing data centers as a by-right use.

dockets.what: Biennial review final order (Nov 25, 2025): created a new GS-5 rate class for customers of 25 MW or more (mostly data centers) from Jan 1, 2027, with 14-year contracts and minimum payments of at least 85% of contracted transmission/distribution demand and 60% of generation demand; approved $565.7M (2026) and $209.9M (2027) rate increases; told Dominion to study shifting more data center costs away from homes.
